experiment.cpu_fallback: torch.profiler capture of the same baseline and fixed steps on the CPU, aten ops classified by self time, uninstrumented before/after step times, and the lab's analyze() on the shipped simulated trace
experiment.title: Lab 4 L2: capture, classify and analyse a real training step (before and after the fixes)

log: baseline step median    36.54 ms  p95    52.37 ms  launches/step 0  syncs/step 0
fixed    step median    34.25 ms  p95    54.94 ms  launches/step 0  syncs/step 0
notes: CPU fallback: torch limited to 4 threads; step time = median of >= 5 steps (perf_counter).
The shipped trace is the lab's SIMULATED ORION capture; it is analysed here only to exercise the pipeline in the GPU image.

findings.evidence: 4 large copies from pageable memory, 200 MiB, 17.7 ms total at 11.8 GB/s vs 48.1 GB/s for pinned; host thread blocked and no kernel overlaps them
findings.recommendation: Pin the source buffers (DataLoader pin_memory=True or a pinned staging pool), copy with non_blocking=True on a side stream one step ahead, and make the compute stream wait on an event.

findings.evidence: 15 host-sync gaps per step, 4.84 ms GPU idle per step; the CPU blocks on .item()/synchronize and the GPU drains before new work arrives
findings.recommendation: Remove the per-layer debug .item() hook; accumulate metrics on the GPU and read them once every N steps; time steps with CUDA events instead of cudaDeviceSynchronize.

findings.evidence: 600 kernels/step shorter than 10 µs (median 2.6 µs, grids of 4 blocks on a 132-SM GPU); 600 launch-bound gaps/step totalling 4.03 ms
findings.recommendation: Use fused/foreach optimizer kernels (multi-tensor apply), flatten small parameters into one buffer, or capture the optimizer step in a CUDA Graph.

findings.evidence: 1 gap(s)/step totalling 0.31 ms where the next kernel (layer_norm_fwd_kernel) had been submitted long before the GPU went idle: the compute stream was waiting on an event from another stream
findings.recommendation: Find the cudaStreamWaitEvent/cudaLaunchHostFunc pair (here a monitoring callback) and take the host function off the compute stream's dependency chain (record an event and poll it later).

findings.evidence: layernorm_bwd_fused_kernel: theoretical occupancy 12.5% (limited by registers), memory-bound at 22% of its roof, 5.0% of kernel time
findings.recommendation: Reduce register pressure (launch bounds / maxrregcount, split the fused kernel) or use smaller blocks so more warps are resident to hide memory latency; re-measure with ncu.
